speaker: Narrator
text: You follow the flitting tūī through the forest until the trees begin to thin out.

speaker: You
text: Where is it going?

speaker: Narrator
text: You step out of the trees and find yourself standing outside a small conservation centre.

speaker: You
text: A conservation centre?

speaker: Narrator
text: The tūī lands on the roof before flying through an open window.

speaker: You
text: Hey! Wait for me!

speaker: Narrator
text: As you approach the building, you faintly hear the familiar melody from the forest.

speaker: You
text: Huh... that music again.

speaker: Narrator
text: You walk inside.

speaker: Helper
text: Oh, hello. Can I help you?

speaker: You
text: I... think so.

speaker: Helper
text: You look a little lost.

speaker: You
text: I followed a hedgehog into the forest. Then I met a talking tūī.

speaker: Helper
text: ...A talking tūī?

speaker: You
text: Yeah.

speaker: Helper
text: Right. Of course.

speaker: You
text: It told me about habitat fragmentation.

speaker: Helper
text: Well then, technically you've come to the right place.

speaker: You
text: What do you mean?

speaker: Helper
text: We work with local Auckland wildlife and help people understand the problems they face.

speaker: Helper
text: Actually, we have something that might help you understand what your so-called tūī was talking about.

speaker: Narrator
text: The helper points towards a familiar-looking box sitting on a table.

speaker: You
text: Wait... that box?

speaker: Helper
text: You were supposed to deliver it, weren't you?

speaker: You
text: Yeah. I was taking it here for my grandmother. But how did it get here? I left it in my car...

speaker: You
text: With MONTY. OH NO. I LEFT MONTY IN MY CAR!

speaker: Helper
text: Well, it looks like they both made it!

speaker: Monty
text: WOOF WOOF. WOOF.

speaker: You
text: MONTY! I'm so sorry. Are you okay?

speaker: Monty
text: Woof.

speaker: You
text: I'll never leave you in a car alone again, I promise.

speaker: Monty
text: Woof woof woof.

speaker: You
text: What's inside the box anyways?

speaker: Helper
text: A few things about the wildlife around here.

speaker: Helper
text: There's also a little puzzle inside. It shows how habitat fragmentation affects different animals.

speaker: You
text: So the box was supposed to teach me about this?

speaker: Helper
text: Maybe your grandmother knew you'd need a little help.

speaker: You
text: She probably did.

speaker: Narrator
text: The helper opens the box and takes out a strange-looking set of tiles.

speaker: You
text: What am I supposed to do with those?

speaker: Helper
text: Think of the tiles as pieces of an animal's habitat.

speaker: Helper
text: When roads, buildings, or other obstacles break up a habitat, animals can have trouble moving between the pieces.

speaker: You
text: So the puzzle is about putting their habitat back together?

speaker: Helper
text: Exactly.

speaker: Helper
text: Each puzzle starts with the habitat completely jumbled up. Your job is to swap the tiles until they form one continuous pathway.

speaker: You
text: How do I swap them?

speaker: Helper
text: Just click on the tiles you want to swap.

speaker: Helper
text: You'll need to arrange them in consecutive order, from the beginning of the pathway to the end.

speaker: You
text: Is there a time limit?

speaker: Helper
text: Nope. Take as much time as you need.

speaker: Helper
text: The point isn't to be fast. It's to understand how fragmented habitats can be connected again.

speaker: You
text: Okay... so what's the first puzzle?

speaker: Helper
text: The first one is about the long-tailed bat, or pekapeka-roa.

speaker: Helper
text: It's a 3 by 3 grid, so it's the easier of the two.

speaker: You
text: And the second one?

speaker: Helper
text: The second is about īnanga. That one is a 4 by 4 grid, so you'll have quite a few more pieces to organise.

speaker: You
text: So... easy first or straight into the hard one?

speaker: Helper
text: It's up to you, but the hard mode is very challenging. I have to warn you. Once you begin a puzzle, you must complete it to continue.

speaker: You
text: Okay. I'll keep that in mind.
